_comment: How a word of a text in Moroccan Arabic (Darija, in Arabic letters) is turned into something a dictionary can be asked about: the Moroccan dictionary first, the standard one after it, these rules and then lib/lang/ar.lookup.json's. Written onto a word standard Arabic also has: the present's ka-/ta- (كيكتب, تيكتب, كنكتب = أكتب: Moroccan's first person singular is n-), the future's ġa- (غيكتب; غادي is a word of its own), the negation's ma-...-š (ماكيكتبش, three steps, so this file allows three), في ال- fused (فالدار), the pronoun written onto the verb with -l- and the dropped hamza. Words of its own (بزاف, ديال, الدراري) are the Moroccan dictionary's. Latin-letter Darija (Arabizi) is not read. Measured on TODOs/arabic-dialects/ar-mor.txt.

_article: THE ARTICLE IS TAKEN OFF HERE and not in ar.lookup.json: Wiktionary's standard Arabic files a word with its article among its forms, and its dialect dictionaries do not (الولاد, الدراري, للدار found nothing). A verb's prefix leaves three letters at least (`min_stem_length`): حالك is not the future's ح + الك.
